mainTopic: A סוכה under a tree, and a סוכה on top of another סוכה: what makes the roof (סכך) count, and when does something above it ruin it?
overview: The משנה teaches two cases. A סוכה built under a tree is like one built inside a house, so it is פסולה. When one סוכה sits on top of another, the upper one is כשרה and the lower one is פסולה, though רבי יהודה says the lower one is כשרה if no one lives in the upper one. רבא limits the tree case to a tree whose shade is greater than its sunlight, and he proves this from the משנה's comparison to a house. רב פפא explains that a sparse tree does not ruin the סוכה when its branches were pressed down into a majority of valid סכך. The גמרא shows that רבא's statement adds something: there is no גזירה against this, and it is allowed even לכתחילה. A ברייתא then learns from the word בסכת, spelled without a ו, that a סוכה under another סוכה is פסולה. Finally, רבי ירמיה lists four outcomes for stacked סוכות, and the גמרא begins explaining each one, depending on shade versus sun and the twenty-אמה height limit. The explanation of the third case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A סוכה Built Under a Tree
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a סוכה built under a tree is treated as if it were built inside a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone builds his סוכה under a tree, it is as if he built it inside a house.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first case: a סוכה under a tree is treated like a סוכה inside a house, which is not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה must have its own סכך directly over it, with nothing blocking it from the sky. A tree hanging over the סוכה blocks it, just like a house's ceiling. The משנה does not simply say 'פסולה'. It uses a comparison to a house, and the גמרא will soon draw a proof from that choice of words.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the base text being studied)
The temporary hut used on סוכות

steps.whyThisMatters: The unusual wording 'as if inside the house' becomes the basis for רבא's limitation and proof later in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who makes his sukkah beneath the tree
it is as though he made it inside the house.
phrases.notes: Meaning it is invalid, like a sukkah under a roof.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה under a tree is like one inside a house, and is invalid.

steps.title: One סוכה Built on Top of Another
steps.stepSummary: When one סוכה is built on top of another, the upper one is valid and the lower one is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a סוכה on top of another סוכה, the top one is כשרה and the bottom one is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case: two סוכות stacked one above the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper סוכה is open to the sky, so it is fine. The lower סוכה has the upper סוכה blocking it from above, much like the tree in the first case. So the lower one is invalid.

phrases.english: A sukkah on top of a sukkah
the upper one is valid
and the lower one is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case of the same משנה, with the same idea that something above the סוכה blocks it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In stacked סוכות, the upper is valid and the lower is invalid.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: The Lower סוכה Can Be Valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the upper סוכה has no residents, the lower one is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if no one lives in the upper סוכה, then the lower one is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion about the lower סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the upper structure only ruins the lower סוכה if it is a real dwelling with people living in it. If it is not lived in, it does not count as a 'roof' over the lower סוכה. The גמרא will define 'no residents' later.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion here

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two cases. A סוכה under a tree is like one inside a house, so it is פסול. With stacked סוכות, the upper is כשרה and the lower is פסולה. רבי יהודה says the lower is כשרה if the upper has no residents.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
if there are no residents in the upper one
the lower one is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the ruling that the lower סוכה is always invalid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the upper סוכה is not lived in, the lower סוכה is valid.

steps.title: רבא Limits the Tree Case
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the tree only invalidates the סוכה if its shade is greater than its sunlight; otherwise the סוכה is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבא said: The משנה only meant a tree whose shade is more than its sunlight. But if its sunlight is more than its shade, the סוכה is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with רבא. He narrows the משנה's first rule about a tree to one specific situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tree is thick enough to make more shade than sun on its own, the tree is doing the shading, not the סכך, so the סוכה is פסול. If the tree is sparse and lets in more sun than shade, the סוכה's own סכך is what makes the shade, so the סוכה is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
They only taught [this ruling] in the case of…

steps.confusionAlert: 'Shade greater than sunlight' here describes the TREE by itself: are its branches thick enough to shade more than half? It is not describing the סוכה's own סכך.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava said:
They taught this only regarding a tree
whose shade is greater than its sunlight,
but if its sunlight is greater than its shade
it is valid.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree only invalidates the סוכה when the tree's shade is greater than its sunlight.

steps.title: Proof From the משנה's Comparison to a House
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבא's source and finds it in the משנה's wording 'as if inside the house': a tree is like a house, whose shade is greater than its sunlight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where does רבא learn this? From the fact that the משנה says 'as if he made it inside the house.' Why say that? It could just have said 'פסולה'! So it must be teaching that a tree is like a house: just as a house has more shade than sun, the tree here also has more shade than sun.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבא's source. It answers that the משנה's extra wording, comparing the tree to a house, supports him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have said 'פסולה' in one word. It chose to compare the tree to a house, so the comparison must be teaching something. A house's roof gives more shade than sun, so the tree that invalidates must be similar, with more shade than sun.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it to teach…?
This is what it teaches us

phrases.english: From where? From the fact that it teaches:
"as though he made it inside the house":
Why do I need it to teach
"as though he made it inside the house"?
Let it teach "invalid"!
Rather, this is what it teaches us:
that a tree is similar to a house:
just as a house, its shade is greater than its sunlight
so too a tree, its shade is greater than its sunlight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבא's limitation.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that only a tree with more shade than sun invalidates the סוכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's extra wording 'כאילו עשאה בתוך הבית' instead of simply 'פסולה'.

steps.title: Challenge: The Tree's Branches Should Mix In and Ruin the Good סכך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: even if the tree is sparse, its attached branches are invalid סכך that combine with the valid סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if the tree has more sunlight than shade, so what? The invalid סכך (the tree's branches) is joining together with the valid סכך!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's ruling that a sparse tree leaves the סוכה כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branches still attached to a tree are סכך פסול. Even if the tree is sparse, its branches are mixed in with the סוכה's valid סכך, so the roof is a combination of good and bad material. Why, then, should the סוכה be valid?

keyTerms.meaning: Invalid roofing material (for example, things still attached to the ground)

phrases.english: And when its sunlight is greater than its shade,
what of it?
Behold, invalid roofing is joining
together with valid roofing!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי חֲמָתוֹ מְרוּבָּה מִצִּלָּתוֹ מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of רבא's statement (the 'כשרה' ruling).
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the סוכה is כשרה when the tree has more sun than shade.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The attached tree branches are סכך פסול mixed with the סכך כשר, which should still invalidate the סוכה.

steps.title: רב פפא: The Branches Were Pressed Down and Mixed In
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that רבא is talking about a case where the tree branches were pressed down and mixed into the valid סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is a case where he pressed the branches down and mixed them in.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by describing the exact case רבא meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person bent the tree's branches down and mixed them into the valid סכך, so they are not a separate layer. Since most of the סכך is valid, the few attached branches become insignificant within it, and the סוכה stays כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the challenge
Where he pressed them down / mixed them in

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: a tree only ruins a סוכה if the tree by itself gives more shade than sun, learned from the משנה's comparison to a house. When the tree is sparse, רב פפא explains that the branches were pressed down into the valid סכך, so they do not ruin it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea of סכך: a minority of invalid material that is fully mixed into valid סכך does not ruin it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Where he pressed them down [into the valid roofing].

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tree branches sit as a separate layer and combine with the valid סכך to ruin it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The branches were pressed down and mixed into a majority of valid סכך, so they do not ruin it.

steps.title: Why would רבא need to say this?
steps.stepSummary: If the branches were pressed down and mixed in, the ruling seems obvious, so why did רבא need to state it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If this is a case where he pressed the branches down, what is there to say? Isn't it obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's explanation. If the branches were pressed down and mixed into the valid סכך, of course the סוכה is valid, so why would רבא bother saying it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the tree branches are mixed in and the valid סכך is the majority, the invalid branches are cancelled out (בטל). That seems so basic that a statement from רבא looks unnecessary. The question is whether רבא's statement adds anything at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He pressed them down, meaning he bent the branches down and mixed them into the סכך
What is there to say? Meaning, it is obvious

phrases.english: If it is where he pressed them down
what is there to say? (It is obvious!)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's answer by saying it makes רבא's statement unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement as explained by רב פפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the branches are mixed in and cancelled out, the validity of the סוכה is obvious, so there was no need for רבא to say it.

steps.title: We do not make a גזירה
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought we should forbid the pressed-down case because of the case where the branches were not pressed down. רבא teaches that we do not make that גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us make a decree and forbid the case where he pressed them down, because of the case where he did not press them down. So רבא teaches us that we do not make that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא's statement does add something. We might have expected the חכמים to forbid even pressed-down branches, so people would not confuse it with branches that were not pressed down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branches that are not pressed down stay separate and invalidate the סוכה. Because the two cases look alike, one could think the חכמים would forbid both as a precaution. רבא teaches that there is no such גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. It introduces a mistaken assumption
Let us decree, a rabbinic precautionary ban
Because of, out of concern for confusion with

phrases.english: You might have said:
let us decree against where he pressed them down
because of where he did not press them down
it teaches us that we do not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 by showing what new idea רבא's statement teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement is needed to reject a possible גזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would make a גזירה against pressed-down branches because of branches that are not pressed down.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not make that גזירה. Pressed-down branches that are cancelled out are fine.

steps.title: A משנה about trellised vines already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says we already learned this in a משנה. If vines are trellised over a סוכה it is invalid, but if the סכך is more than the vines, or the vines were cut, it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too we already learned in a משנה: If he trained a grapevine, a gourd plant, or ivy over the סוכה and put סכך on top of them, it is invalid. But if the סכך was more than the plants, or he cut them, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again and says רבא's lesson is already in a משנה. It quotes the משנה to set up the proof, and the next step shows how the proof works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plants still attached to the ground are invalid סכך. The משנה says the סוכה is still valid if the valid סכך is more than the attached plants. That looks like the same rule רבא taught, which would make his statement unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: This too we have already learned (in a משנה)
He trained or trellised a climbing plant over something
He cut them, so they are no longer attached to the ground

phrases.english: This too we have learned:
If he trellised over it

phrases.aramaic: אֶת הַגֶּפֶן וְאֶת הַדְּלַעַת וְאֶת הַקִּיסוֹס,
phrases.english: the grapevine, the gourd, or the ivy
and put roofing on top of them — it is invalid
but if the roofing was more than them
or if he cut them — it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 9 but argues that a משנה already teaches it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a משנה already teaches that we make no גזירה, רבא's statement adds nothing.

steps.title: Proving the משנה is about pressed-down plants
steps.stepSummary: The משנה cannot be talking about plants that were not pressed down, because then they would combine with the valid סכך. So it must mean pressed-down plants, which shows we make no גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case in the משנה? If you say he did not press the plants down, then the invalid סכך joins together with the valid סכך! Rather, it must be that he pressed them down. Learn from this that we do not make a גזירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof. It explains why the משנה must be talking about pressed-down plants, so the משנה already teaches רבא's lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the plants stayed separate, they would combine with the valid סכך and the סוכה could not be valid. Since the משנה calls it valid, the plants must have been pressed down and cancelled out. The משנה makes no גזירה against this, which seems to leave רבא with nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What exact case is this?
Learn from it, a conclusion drawn

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If you say it is where he did not press them down

phrases.aramaic: הָא קָא מִצְטָרֵף סְכָךְ פָּסוּל עִם סְכָךְ כָּשֵׁר!
phrases.english: but the invalid roofing joins together with the valid roofing!
Rather, is it not where he pressed them down?
And learn from this that we do not decree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 10 by defining the case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה can only be about pressed-down plants, so it already teaches that there is no גזירה, which makes רבא redundant.

steps.title: רבא teaches it is allowed even לכתחילה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה might only allow it בדיעבד. רבא teaches that it is allowed even לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the משנה's ruling is only after the fact, but you may not do it from the start. So רבא teaches us that it is allowed even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא still adds something. The משנה could be read as allowing this only after it was already done, and רבא teaches that you may set up your סוכה this way from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes a case where someone already built the סוכה and calls it valid. That could mean it is only acceptable after the fact. רבא's statement shows it is fully allowed even before building.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact, once it is already done

steps.whatToRemember: Tree branches that are pressed down and mixed into a majority of valid סכך do not invalidate the סוכה. There is no גזירה against it, and it is allowed even לכתחילה.

phrases.english: You might have said:
this applies only after the fact
but not from the start
it teaches us (that even from the start it is allowed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 10-11 by showing what רבא adds beyond the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows pressed-down plants only בדיעבד.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא teaches it is allowed even לכתחילה.

steps.title: Source for invalidating a סוכה under a סוכה, a tree, or a house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה of סוכה על גבי סוכה and brings a ברייתא. It reads the פסוק 'בסכת תשבו' to exclude a סוכה beneath another סוכה, beneath a tree, or inside a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a סוכה on top of a סוכה, and so on. The חכמים taught in a ברייתא: 'In סוכות you shall dwell.' This excludes a סוכה beneath another סוכה, a סוכה beneath a tree, and a סוכה inside a house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting the opening words of the next part of the משנה. Then it brings a ברייתא that gives the source in the תורה for why a lower סוכה is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the פסוק that a סוכה must be open to the sky, with nothing covering its סכך. A second סוכה, a tree, or a house roof above it makes it invalid. This gives the תורה basis for the משנה's ruling and connects back to the earlier discussion of trees.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים taught, which introduces a ברייתא
You shall dwell (from the פסוק about סוכות)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's exclusion depends on the word בסכת, read as 'one סוכה' and not one stacked under another. That is why the next step attacks this word as plural, and step 15 defends it from its spelling. The parentheses are only a printing note on the word.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule that the סכך must be the only cover between you and the sky. It explains why a סוכה under a tree or a roof does not count.

phrases.english: A sukka on top of a sukka, etc.
The Sages taught:
"In sukkot you shall dwell"
and not in a sukka that is beneath a sukka
and not in a sukka that is beneath a tree
and not in a sukka that is inside a house.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוכה על גבי סוכה וכו׳ תנו רבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the tree-branch discussion and opens a new section on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's ruling that the lower סוכה of two stacked סוכות is invalid
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the פסוק 'בסכת תשבו' (ויקרא כג:מב)

steps.title: The word looks plural, so it should allow two סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the word בסוכות is plural, so it should include a סוכה under a סוכה rather than exclude it.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! 'בסוכות' (in סוכות) means two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא from the last step. The ברייתא used 'בסכת' to exclude a סוכה under a סוכה, but the word sounds plural, which suggests two סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא read the פסוק as 'one סוכה, not one under another.' The challenge flips this around: a plural word should teach that even two stacked סוכות are fine. The word אדרבה signals that the proof points the opposite way.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is true

phrases.english: On the contrary:
phrases.notes: Signals that the evidence points the opposite way

phrases.english: 'In sukkot' means two!
phrases.notes: The plural should include a סוכה on top of a סוכה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's derivation from 'בסכת תשבו' excluding a סוכה under a סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is plural, which implies two סוכות, so it should permit stacked סוכות, not forbid them.

steps.title: The word is written without a ו, meaning one סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the word is spelled בסכת, without a ו, so it reads as singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is written 'בסכת' (without the letter ו).
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends the ברייתא. He points out that the spelling of the word in the תורה has no ו, so it can be read as a single סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pronunciation is plural, but the written spelling (כתיב) is missing the ו that would make it clearly plural. The ברייתא learns from the written form: one סוכה, not one stacked on another. This saves the ברייתא's exclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (how the word is spelled in the תורה)
Spelled without the ו, so it can be read as singular
The אמורא who gives this answer

steps.confusionAlert: The word is pronounced as a plural, but here we learn from how it is spelled. The missing ו is what makes it read as 'one סוכה.'

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
'Basukkot' is written (without a vav).
phrases.notes: The spelling reads as one סוכה

steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: the written spelling (כתיב) overrides the plural pronunciation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural sound of the word would teach that two stacked סוכות are fine
steps.terutzMaskana: The word is written without a ו, so it means one סוכה and excludes a סוכה under a סוכה

steps.title: Four possible outcomes for two stacked סוכות
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says that with two stacked סוכות, sometimes both are fit, sometimes both are unfit, sometimes only the lower one is fit, and sometimes only the upper one is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Sometimes both are fit; sometimes both are unfit; sometimes the lower is fit and the upper is unfit; sometimes the lower is unfit and the upper is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives a list of four possibilities for one סוכה built on top of another. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא explains each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made it sound like the lower סוכה is always פסולה. רבי ירמיה shows the result depends on the details, such as whether there is more shade than sun and how high the upper roof is. He gives only the list here, and the explanations come next.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'סוכה על גבי סוכה' is not one simple rule. Each stacked setup has to be checked on its own details.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
There are times when both are fit,
times when both are unfit,
times when the lower is fit and the upper is unfit,
and times when the lower is unfit and the upper is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: פְּעָמִים שֶׁשְּׁתֵּיהֶן כְּשֵׁירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the source, the גמרא turns to the practical details of stacked סוכות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether stacked סוכות are fit depends on the case. There are four possible combinations.

steps.title: When both stacked סוכות are fit
steps.stepSummary: Both are fit when the lower roof has more sun than shade, the upper roof has more shade than sun, and the upper roof is within twenty אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When are both fit? For example, when the lower one has more sun than shade, and the upper one has more shade than sun, and the upper one stands within twenty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first of רבי ירמיה's cases: how both סוכות can be כשרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lower roof has more sun than shade, so it does not count as a real סכך and is not considered a separate סוכה. The upper roof is valid and lower than twenty אמות from the lower floor, so it serves as the סכך for both. This means nobody is truly sitting 'under another סוכה.'

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
Its sunlight is more than its shade, so it is פסולה
Its shade is more than its sunlight, so it is כשרה

steps.confusionAlert: Here the lower סוכה becomes כשרה because its own roof does NOT count. That leaves the upper roof as its only real roof.

phrases.english: Times when both are fit: what are the circumstances?
For example, where the lower one's sunlight is greater than its shade,
phrases.notes: So the lower roof does not count as סכך

phrases.english: and the upper one's shade is greater than its sunlight,
and the upper one stands within twenty (אמות).
phrases.notes: So the upper roof works for both סוכות

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first case in רבי ירמיה's list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What setup makes both stacked סוכות fit?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lower roof has more sun than shade, upper roof has more shade than sun, and the upper roof is within twenty אמות

steps.title: When both stacked סוכות are unfit
steps.stepSummary: Both are unfit when both roofs have more shade than sun, but the upper one is more than twenty אמות high.
steps.simpleTranslation: When are both unfit? For example, when both have more shade than sun, and the upper one stands higher than twenty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second case: how both סוכות can be פסולות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper סוכה is פסולה because its roof is above twenty אמות, which is too high. The lower one has a proper roof of its own, but it sits under the upper roof, which still covers it. So the lower one is a סוכה under a סוכה and is also פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Higher than twenty אמות, too tall for a valid סוכה

steps.whatToRemember: With stacked סוכות, check two things: whether each roof has more shade than sun, and whether the upper roof is within twenty אמות. These details decide which סוכה is fit.

phrases.english: Times when both are unfit: what are the circumstances?
For example, where in both, their shade is greater than their sunlight,
and the upper one stands above twenty cubits.
phrases.notes: Upper is too high; lower is under another סוכה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second case in רבי ירמיה's list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What setup makes both stacked סוכות unfit?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both roofs have more shade than sun, but the upper is above twenty אמות. The upper is too high, and the lower is under another סוכה.

steps.title: Third case: lower סוכה fit, upper סוכה unfit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the third of רבי ירמיה's four cases: a situation where only the lower סוכה is כשר and the upper one is פסול. The details come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are times when the lower סוכה is fit and the upper סוכה is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is moving to the third of רבי ירמיה's four cases and names its result: the lower סוכה works and the upper one doesn't. This is a setup line, and the next line will explain what the case looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 17 and 18 explained the first two cases: both fit, and both unfit. Now the result flips between the two סוכות, so one is good and the other is not. The only new information here is the result itself. The physical setup that produces it, meaning how much shade each roof gives and how high each one is, is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfit; not valid for the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the reason in this line. It only names the result, and the next line of the גמרא gives the case that explains it.

phrases.english: There are times when the lower one is fit
phrases.notes: Third of רבי ירמיה's four possibilities

phrases.english: and the upper one is unfit

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the second case (both unfit, step 18) to the third case in רבי ירמיה's list from step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Names the third case's result: the lower סוכה is fit and the upper סוכה is unfit. The specific conditions follow in the next line.
